title: Controlling Audio from Scripts
description: Play, stop, and manage AudioSources dynamically with C#. Use PlayOneShot and PlayClipAtPoint for one‑time effects.

slides.title: Getting a Reference to AudioSource 🔌
slides.content:
# The Scripting Entry Point

To control audio via code, you need a reference to the AudioSource component:

```csharp
AudioSource audioSource = GetComponent<AudioSource>();
```

Or if you have a public field, drag the AudioSource from the Inspector.

You can then call methods on it: `Play()`, `Stop()`, `Pause()`, `UnPause()`.

quizData.question: Which method resumes a paused AudioSource?
quizData.explanation: UnPause() continues playback from where it was paused.

slides.title: Basic Playback Control ▶️⏸️
slides.content:
# Playing, Stopping, Pausing

- `audioSource.Play()` – starts playing the assigned clip.
- `audioSource.Stop()` – stops playback (resets position to beginning).
- `audioSource.Pause()` – pauses at current position.
- `audioSource.UnPause()` – continues from where it paused.

You can check `audioSource.isPlaying` to see if it's currently playing.

Example: toggle music on/off with a key.

slides.title: PlayOneShot & PlayClipAtPoint 🎯
slides.content:
# One‑Time Sound Effects

Sometimes you want to play a sound without a dedicated AudioSource component. Two handy methods:

- `audioSource.PlayOneShot(AudioClip clip, float volumeScale)` – plays a clip on top of the AudioSource's existing clip, without interrupting it. Perfect for overlapping footstep sounds.
- `AudioSource.PlayClipAtPoint(AudioClip clip, Vector3 position, float volume)` – creates a temporary GameObject at a position, plays the sound, and then destroys it. Great for impact sounds at a specific location (3D).

Both are static/instance methods that simplify one‑shot effects.

quizData.question: What does PlayOneShot allow you to do?

options.text: Play an additional clip without stopping the current one

quizData.explanation: PlayOneShot plays another clip while the main clip continues.

slides.title: Changing Volume & Pitch at Runtime 🎚️
slides.content:
# Dynamic Adjustments

You can modify properties directly in script:
- `audioSource.volume = 0.5f;`
- `audioSource.pitch = 1.2f;`
- `audioSource.spatialBlend = 1f;`

These changes take effect immediately. You can smoothly fade audio by interpolating volume in `Update()` using `Mathf.Lerp`.

Example: fade out music.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## AudioSource Pooling

Instantiating many temporary AudioSources can hit performance. For frequent sounds, create a pool of reusable AudioSources and cycle through them.
